title: Customer Ask Consolidator and Timebox Acceptance Engine
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Top customers and strategic prospects frequently submit high-impact feature asks through multiple channels (Support, Sales, CSMs, Slack). Current intake is fragmented: PMs manually triage, engineering gets ad-hoc RFCs mid-cycle, and commitments are made without a consistent timebox or trade-off signal. This creates unpredictable scope creep, missed SLAs for enterprise accounts, and difficulty quantifying risk-to-commitment for roadmap negotiations.

Proposal: Build a Customer Ask Consolidator (CAC) paired with a Timebox Acceptance Engine (TAE). CAC aggregates signals from CRM, support tickets, account execs, and the customer success priority form into a normalized request record. TAE applies a configurable policy surface (account weight, revenue tier, E2E risk, engineering effort estimate, latency/cost impact) to produce a recommendation: Accept (with sprint window), Defer, or Accept-Partial (timeboxed MVP + roadmap backlog). The output feeds into the roadmap intake queue and creates a structured commitment ledger in the Redwood Console.

Why now: Increasing Dedicated and Private sales cycles require explicit delivery commitments. Sales and CSMs are escalating asks directly to engineering leads. A system that standardizes acceptance rules and surfaces trade-offs reduces negotiation overhead, aligns expectations, and creates measurable OKR-linked commitments.

Scope: MVP will include: 1) a normalized intake schema and UI form, 2) a policy engine with pluggable heuristics (account score, estimated effort, customer SLO tier), 3) UI in Console for PMs/Sales to review recommendations, 4) audit logs and commitment ledger export, 5) webhook to create a canonical Linear ticket with prefilled metadata and priority. Exclusions: full automated acceptance and billing contract changes (post-MVP).
acceptance_criteria: CAC ingests and normalizes requests from: Salesforce Opportunity notes, Zendesk ticket tag 'top-account-ask', CSM intake form, and dedicated-sales email alias (proof-of-concept connectors).

TAE policy panel in Console allows PMs to set weights for account score, revenue tier, engineering effort, latency impact, and legal/compliance flag. Changes in weights produce visible re-ranking in the intake queue.
For 100 sample historically escalated asks, TAE's recommendation matches the historical outcome (Accept/Defer/Partial) >= 75% after one week of manual calibration.
Webhook creates a Linear ticket with key prefix PM- and populates: title, customer, recommended decision, rationale, estimated points, and initial assignee suggestion.
Commitment ledger entries appear in Console with timestamp, decision, requester, and rollback triggers; entries can be exported as CSV for quarterly OKR reconciliation.
Audit logs capture reviewer, votes, and comments for every accepted or partially accepted request for compliance and renewal discussions.
notes: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Sales, CSM, Eng, Design. Agreed on canonical fields for intake schema (customer, ARR tier, feature summary, business impact, urgency, regulatory constraints, suggested priority). Action: Sales to provide 50 sample requests by 2026-03-01. (Owner: Hannah Park)

2026-02-28: Design sketch reviewed. Marco Ruiz proposed a two-pane Console experience: 'Incoming' queue + 'Decision review' modal. Highlight: show cost/latency delta estimates per ask using Redwood Optimize heuristics (deferred).

2026-03-03: Engineering spike planned to validate connectors (Salesforce -> CAC, Zendesk -> CAC). ENG spike PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7983 (spike branch). Liam to estimate integration effort after spike (ETA 5 days).

2026-03-08: PM review with VP Product (Priya Singh). Priya recommended conservative default for account weight to avoid oversubscribing dev capacity. Decision: default account weight set to 0.6; release can override per-queue. Recorded in Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/326589-CAC-TAE-PRD

2026-03-10: UX critique: include quick-override badges (Legal Hold, Security Flag) that short-circuit acceptance and require manual review. Design to add prominent banner and checklist. Action: DES-993 to add banner states.

Risks: 1) Overfitting policy to historical noisy labels — mitigated by weekly calibration window and human-in-loop override. 2) Sales asks bypassing CAC — mitigated by routing policy and admin training (CSM playbook).

Next steps: finish connector spike (ENG), build policy engine stub, wire minimal Console UI, run 6-week pilot with 3 top accounts (Alpha customers), track metrics: time-to-decision, %accepted, downstream engineering rework, and renewal sentiment.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha, 6 weeks): pilot with 3 accounts, manual review required for all accepts; measure decision latency and acceptance accuracy. Phase 2 (Beta, 3 months): add automated connectors, enable default weights for low-risk accounts, allow Sales to submit through Console form; instrument commitment ledger. Phase 3 (GA): integrate with contract change flow and allow engineering to tag accepted items as 'committed' for sprint planning and OKR linking. Canary: start with non-blocking UI flags; promote to forced gating after 8 weeks if metrics satisfy SLOs (time-to-decision < 48h for 80% of requests, commit accuracy > 70%).
